question.prompt:
In square \(ABCD,\) points \(E\) and \(H\) lie on \(\overline{AB}\) and \(\overline{DA},\) respectively, so that \(AE=AH.\) Points \(F\) and \(G\) lie on \(\overline{BC}\) and \(\overline{CD},\) respectively, and points \(I\) and \(J\) lie on \(\overline{EH}\) so that \(\overline{FI} \perp \overline{EH}\) and \(\overline{GJ} \perp \overline{EH}.\) See the figure below. Triangle \(AEH,\) quadrilateral \(BFIE,\) quadrilateral \(DHJG,\) and pentagon \(FCGJI\) each has area \(1.\) What is \(FI^2?\)

[Figure 1](figures/2020_AMC_10B_Q21_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
[Figure 1](figures/2020_AMC_10B_Q21_question_fig1.svg)

The four given regions partition the square, so its area is \(4\) and its side length is \(2\). Since \(AE=AH\) and the angle at \(A\) is a right angle, the area of \(\triangle AEH\) gives
\[
\frac{AE^2}{2}=1,
\qquad AE=AH=\sqrt2.
\]
Consequently,
\[
BE=2-\sqrt2>0.
\]

To relate the quadrilateral's area directly to \(FI^2\), extend \(HE\) beyond \(E\) to meet the line \(BC\) at \(K\). This point lies beyond \(B\), on the side away from \(C\).

Triangle \(AEH\) is right isosceles, so \(EH\) makes a \(45^\circ\) angle with the square's sides. Therefore \(\triangle BEK\) has angles \(45^\circ,45^\circ,90^\circ\), giving
\[
BK=BE=2-\sqrt2.
\]
Also, \(KI\) lies on \(EH\), \(FI\perp EH\), and \(KF\) lies along \(BC\). Thus \(\triangle KFI\) is right isosceles with equal perpendicular legs \(KI=FI\), so its area is \(FI^2/2\).

Removing \(\triangle KBE\) from \(\triangle KFI\) leaves exactly quadrilateral \(BFIE\), whose area is \(1\). Hence
\[
\frac{FI^2}{2}
=1+\frac{(2-\sqrt2)^2}{2}.
\]
Multiplying by \(2\) and expanding gives
\[
FI^2=2+(2-\sqrt2)^2
=\boxed{8-4\sqrt2},
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{B}\).
solutions.title: Complete the quadrilateral to a right isosceles triangle
